title: Exact Quantum Algorithms for Composed Boolean Functions Break Pointer-Function Exponents
whyItMatters: With main proof ideas generated by GPT-6 Astra, closed the recursive not-all-equal exact quantum query gap and proved nearly quadratic total-function randomized-vs-exact quantum separations (breaking the classic 3/2 exponent).
summary: Gagan Chiruvella, Chandrima Kayal, Rajat Mittal, Manaswi Paraashar, and Nitin Saurabh (arXiv:2611.16412, Nov 2026)—explicitly crediting OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 with generating the main proof ideas—proved a general coherent error-correction composition theorem for exact (zero-error) quantum query algorithms. By coherently correcting approximate inner block evaluations, they showed composed exact algorithms cost roughly the polynomial degree of the outer function times the bounded-error inner query cost—closing the 13-year gap on Ambainis’s recursive not-all-equal function and pushing total-function randomized-vs-exact quantum query and communication separations from exponent 3/2 up to nearly quadratic (2 − o(1)).
technicalHighlights: Proved a coherent error-correction composition theorem showing exact quantum query complexity need not compose multiplicatively with exact inner costs.
Closed the longstanding gap between Ambainis’s exact quantum algorithm and adversary lower bounds for the recursive not-all-equal function.
Improved total-function randomized-vs-exact quantum query separation from pointer-function exponent 3/2 to R ≥ Q_E^{2−o(1)} and sensitivity separation from 1.1527 to 3/2−o(1).
caveats: Posted as a November 2026 arXiv preprint under active peer review (already cited and tightened in subsequent November 2026 arXiv follow-ups), with no Lean formalization yet.
